request: Analyze GSE304653 for PMID 42155766 (Exercise suppresses breast cancer and reprograms the immune tumor microenvironment, cancer cell intrinsic features, and their interaction): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.model: Met1-iRFP orthotopic breast tumors in female FVB mice; voluntary wheel running vs sedentary (no wheel) from day 3 after implantation (S2.1.2.p1, S2.2.p1)
final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (KAPA stranded mRNA, HiSeq 50bp PE), STAR mm10 + featureCounts gencode vM18 (S2.4.p1)
final.fractions: tumors digested and flow-sorted into iRFP+ cancer cells and iRFP- TME cells from the same tumors (S2.4.p1, S3.p4)
final.sample_inclusion: TME fraction: exercise n=4 vs sedentary n=4 (FIG2 C); cancer-cell fraction: exercise n=7 vs sedentary n=8 (FIG3 B)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of exercise (wheel running vs sedentary) on gene expression, estimated separately within each sorted fraction: (1) TME iRFP- cells, (2) cancer iRFP+ cells
planned_contrasts: TME iRFP-: Exercise vs Sedentary, DESeq2 (S3.p2, FIG2 C; paper: 87 DEGs at padj < 0.1)
Cancer iRFP+: Exercise vs Sedentary, DESeq2 (S3.p4, FIG3 B; paper: 293 DEGs at padj < 0.1)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none within a fraction (one sample per mouse per fraction); the two fractions come from the same tumors but are analyzed separately
final.paper_method: DESeq2 per fraction, Exercise vs control (S2.4.p1); GSEA on log2FC-ranked genes with mouse Hallmark via genekitr (S2.4.p1); Reactome on up/down DEGs and IPA (S3.p4)

paper_results.named_cancer_genes: HMGB2 targets up: Iqgap3, Cenpe, Cenpf, Dlgap5, Kif23, Kif2c, Mki67, Ncaph (written 'Nacph'), Top2a, Tpx2, Anln, Hmmr; down: Hist3h2a (written 'Hist3ha'). CTF1 targets: down Etfb, Thrsp, Postn; up Plcb4, Med13, Fasn, Tgm2 (S3.p8, S4.p6)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Methods S2.4.p1 define the RNA-seq assay, sorting into iRFP+ and iRFP- fractions, featureCounts counts and DESeq2. Results S3.p2 (TME, 87 DEGs, padj < 0.1, n=4 vs 4 per FIG2 C) and S3.p4 (cancer cells, 293 DEGs, padj < 0.1, n=7 vs 8 per FIG3 B) give two separate exercise-vs-control contrasts. No fold-change cutoff is stated. GEO metadata sample counts match the figure legends exactly.

checks: 23 GEO samples = 15 cancer (8 SED, 7 EX) + 8 TME (4 SED, 4 EX), matching FIG3 B and FIG2 C n
matrix has 23 columns whose names equal the GEO 'Library name' in description
GEO data_processing text is identical to S2.4.p1 (STAR AllBestScore, featureCounts, gencode vM18)

ownership.reasoning: The paper's data availability statement S8.p1 deposits RNA-seq under GSE304653; sample counts and processing text match the paper.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns (CN2..SR10) are the GEO library names in the description column ('Library name: CN2'); exact match on the derived lib key. Fraction and treatment come from the title (GEO spells 'Sendentary'), cross-checked against characteristics cell type/treatment. Library prefixes agree: CN/CR = cancer sedentary/runner, SN/SR = stroma (TME) sedentary/runner. cgrp combines fraction and treatment so each fraction's contrast can be named.

matrix.reasoning: integer_fraction 1.0, max 1.9e6, many zeros; GEO data_processing: featureCounts gencode vM18, 'txt file contains raw gene counts for each sample'; paper feeds counts to DESeq2. Feature IDs are gene symbols.

final.analysis_type: two-group within each fraction (stratified, separate fits)

candidates.value: one joint model over 23 samples with ~ cell + grp + cell:grp
candidates.reason_rejected: the paper fits each sorted fraction separately (FIG2 C n=4/4, FIG3 B n=7/8); fractions have very different expression profiles and dispersions, and pairing of fractions within mouse would need a mouse block the paper does not use

candidates.value: pooled Exercise vs Sedentary over both fractions
candidates.reason_rejected: mixes cell populations; not the paper's estimand

design.reasoning: Paper reports two separate exercise-vs-control analyses, one per sorted fraction (S3.p2, S3.p4). Each is a two-arm comparison of independent mice. All mice are female (S2.1.2.p1); sex check is expected to agree.

candidates.reason_rejected: within a fraction each mouse contributes one sample, so there is nothing to block; the cancer and TME samples of one mouse are never in the same fit

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals randomized to wheel or sedentary (S2.1.2.p1); no batch, sequencing lane or sex variation is recorded in GEO, and the paper's DESeq2 uses treatment only.

final.formula: ~ cgrp (within each fraction subset; equivalent to ~ treatment)

paper_route.reason: pydeseq2 implements the same negative-binomial Wald test

deviations: pydeseq2 port rather than R DESeq2; small numeric differences in dispersion fitting and independent filtering are possible

method.reasoning: Raw featureCounts counts support DESeq2, the paper's stated method (S2.4.p1). alpha = 0.1 matches the paper's padj cutoff for independent filtering.

threshold.reasoning: S3.p2 and S3.p4 (and FIG2 C, FIG3 B): 'p_adj < 0.1', no fold-change rule. Audit rule is the workflow default BH padj < 0.05, labelled separately.

caveats: GSEA via gseapy prerank (log2FC ranking, MSigDB mouse Hallmark) instead of genekitr
paper's Reactome ORA and IPA are not reproduced; GO/KEGG ORA on up/down cancer DEGs is exploratory

study.reasoning: Both planned contrasts follow the paper's sample set, method and threshold. Named genes come from the NicheNet target lists of DEGs in cancer cells (S3.p8, S4.p6); the paper names no individual TME DEGs.

discrepancies.data: GEO extract protocol says 'KAPA Standard mRNA-Seq'
RNA-seq subsets: cancer 7 EX / 8 SED, TME 4 EX / 4 SED, matching FIG2 C and FIG3 B

executions.reasoning: S3.p4 / FIG3 B: cancer-cell (iRFP+) Exercise (n=7) vs Sedentary (n=8), DESeq2, padj < 0.1
